name: homebrew-install
body: Apple silicon and Intel macOS users install via a Homebrew tap: `brew tap really-knows-ai/kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide`, then `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide`, then `brew install kalide` (formula `Formula/kalide.rb`); `brew upgrade kalide` upgrades. The explicit trust step is required by Homebrew 6.0.0+ (June 2026), which refuses to load a formula from an untrusted third-party tap ("Refusing to load formula ... from untrusted tap"); because kalide's tap is added with a custom remote URL (not the default `homebrew/<name>` remote), Homebrew refuses the per-formula `brew trust --formula kalide` form for it, so the tap-level `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` is the form that must be used. The formula downloads the arch-matching binary for the running Mac — `kalide-darwin-arm64` on Apple silicon, `kalide-darwin-amd64` on Intel — from the public GitHub Release of really-knows-ai/kalide using plain release-download `url`s (`https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/kalide-darwin-<arch>`) with `sha256`, fetched anonymously by Homebrew's standard downloader. No custom download strategy and no GitHub account, token or `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN` is involved (trust is a local decision and needs no account). AC: on a clean Mac of either architecture with no GitHub credentials or token env vars set, `brew tap` + `brew trust really-knows-ai/kalide` + `brew install kalide` succeeds and `kalide` runs; `brew install kalide` run before the trust step fails with the untrusted-tap error; `Formula/kalide.rb` contains no `using:`/custom strategy, no `require` of a strategy file, and no reference to `HOMEBREW_GITHUB_API_TOKEN`; `Formula/lib/github_private_release_download_strategy.rb` does not exist.
